## git-commit-guard-hook {#git-commit-guard-hook}

### Guard the git shapes that fail silently in a shared working tree

Several agent sessions commit to one checkout. `git add -A`, `commit -a`, a bare `stash`, and
`--amend` all behave correctly for a single developer and wrongly here: they sweep up, hide or
rewrite another session's work. Each was observed at least once — including a swept file that
reached prod ahead of its own migration. Prose rules did not stop it; a PreToolUse hook does.

Two design rules came out of the false positives: match `git` only at a **command position**, and
**blank quoted spans** before matching, so a `grep "git add -A"` is not a sweep. A guard that fires
on ordinary work teaches the override.

## deploy-gate-hook {#deploy-gate-hook}

### Push and tag only after the owner types "deploy" in that session

Permission `ask` rules did not prompt in auto mode, and a `deny` rule cannot tell that the owner
said "deploy". A UserPromptSubmit hook records the owner's word for one hour; a PreToolUse hook
refuses `git push` / pipeline tag without it. The match is a WHOLE prompt of just "deploy" (optionally
"#N"), so text relayed between agent sessions cannot trip it.

## agent-ssh-is-a-forced-command {#agent-ssh-is-a-forced-command}

### Agents reach prod only through a read-only forced command

The workstation holds the owner's full-power keys. A separate key is bound on the server to a
forced command that can only run a read-only inspection script, and `ssh_guard.php` refuses every
other ssh/scp/sftp/rsync shape and any command naming the owner's keys. The agent gets what it needs
to verify a deploy; it never gets a shell.

## auto-loaded-instruction-budget {#auto-loaded-instruction-budget}

### The auto-loaded instruction files have a byte budget

Every rule added after a failure is reasonable on its own, and none is ever retired, so the
always-loaded files grew past 100 KB — context every session paid for on every turn. A budget that
`kb_index.py --check` enforces turns "should we add this rule here?" into "which rule moves to a
module doc to make room?".

## bucket-e-chores-are-pre-authorized {#bucket-e-chores-are-pre-authorized}

### One bucket where reading the board is permission to start

Everywhere else an agent proposes and waits. Bucket E holds work with exactly one sensible
implementation, so an agent may claim and work it unattended. The admission test is "cannot make a
wrong call about HOW", not "small"; `board.py --check` rejects a chore carrying a blocker or a
verify date, and the moment a chore reveals a fork it is flipped back to `actionable`.
